title: ServiceNow Stock: Buy the Dip? | NOW Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reviews ServiceNow after its post-results plunge, asking whether the dip is a buying opportunity or a time to sell. Revenue topped $4.1 billion, up over 20% year on year, and management raised full-year guidance across the board, yet investors were disappointed and the shares fell. The bright spot was remaining performance obligations, up 22% to $29.7 billion, slightly ahead of revenue growth, which he reads as a sign that growth is sustainable and could accelerate. He argues the February 'SaaS-pocalypse' fear that enterprises would bypass ServiceNow for large language models has not played out: ServiceNow has become the enterprise 'control tower' for AI, with AI annual contract value of $1.7 billion, up 70% since the start of 2026, and agentic-AI consumption up more than 13 times year on year. The disappointments were pedestrian operating cash flow growth ($839 million versus $813 million a year earlier) and a $9 billion-plus acquisition earlier in 2026 that has yet to clearly pay off. At a forward price-to-earnings ratio just under 22, near its cheapest ever, with analysts expecting about 24.5% EPS growth, he sees an attractive setup, and his updated discounted cash flow value is roughly $143. Call: NOW — BUY (reiterated). Bull case: the enterprise AI control-tower position with accelerating agentic adoption. Bear case: weak cash-flow growth and the unproven large acquisition.
